chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Rayyan, from Qasim al-Sayqal, who said:
I did not see anyone who was more strict regarding the shade than Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). He used to order the dome and the two curtains to be removed when he entered the state of Ihram.

key_terms.أَحْرَمَ: He entered the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq do regarding the tent shade when he entered Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the rigorous adherence of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) to the prohibition of head-covering during Ihram, extending beyond the basic requirement to include the removal of the tent's dome and curtains. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *ihtiyat* (precaution) in ritual purity, ensuring that no element of 'covering' (*qubba*) remains, thereby distinguishing the pilgrim's state of humility from worldly comfort. Such strictness underscores the spiritual significance of shedding all forms of adornment and shelter to fully submit to the Divine command.
